title: GtGenerator: one class, one code block per problem, one output per problem
subtitle: The command line calls only the class; the class calls the code of the problem asked for. Each problem keeps its difficult code and its own output together.

entry.label: command line and the class that is its only way in

problem.label: one problem: its generator (hashed), its writer and its output

shared.label: shared: the key and the versions, the raw data and its reader

tool.label: tools that read the output and change nothing of the GT

nodes.label: python -m GtGenerator COMMAND
nodes.note: the parser and ONE call GtGenerator.<method>(**arguments) per command; it imports nothing else of the package (a test pins that); exit 0 done, 1 not there / incomplete, 2 wrong arguments

nodes.label: class GtGenerator: one method per command
nodes.note: api.py = the static methods (generate, generate_bev_gt, generate_lane_gt, gt_key, have, check_data, audit_lane, area_masks, sets, versions, view, video, check, report, digest, clean, selftest ...), suite.py = the class (it is also the object that makes the GT of one keyframe), __init__.py = the names of the package (lazy: nothing is imported until a name is asked for, so the job runner can read JOBS without numpy), jobs.py = the two generation calls as jobs of autoresearch/jobrunner (JOBS, and the small class of the same name that the job runner builds); AutoGT is the old name

nodes.label:
GT key and versions
what did I get?
nodes.note: GtKey = the data identity + per part (front / lane / masks) the code signature, store, version, git commit, dirty; complete is judged by the files that are there; versions.csv maps a signature to a version (new rows are derived from git: versions --update); same_gt_as and the pinned digests prove that new code makes the same GT; gt_api.py also has generate_bev_gt / generate_lane_gt, which call the problems below

nodes.label:
Front GT: map, boxes, flow
-> <sig>/<token>.npz
nodes.note: BEV layers, objects, velocity / flow in m/s and coverage masks per keyframe. The six hashed files make the front signature (6a7aa7864a, v9): editing one needs a version row and a rebuild of the BEV GT cache. pipeline.py writes the files (groups of 60 sequences, resumable, workers), store.py keeps the files and the index.json manifest (complete, scenes, stride, commit, dirty, release, data identity)

nodes.label:
Lane GT: graph, tiers
-> lane/<sig>/<token>.pkl.gz
nodes.note: the lane graph, roads, lines, areas, tiers and camera visibility per point, for lane_center (Spurmitte) and bev_fusion; the six hashed files of the lane signature; its writer and its store code are inside lane_gt.py (the difficult code stays local)

nodes.label:
Area masks (BEV grid)
-> lane/<sig>/masks/*.npz
nodes.note: exact cell-centre raster of the lane polygons into the BEV grid, packed per frame next to the lane store; derived from the lane GT, not hashed

nodes.label:
Look, check, tidy
view, video, report, clean, audit
nodes.note: consistency checks, one PDF over all sequences, pictures, H.264 video, lane graph pictures, clean (never a released store), audit of a stored lane GT before its release

nodes.label:
Raw nuScenes + reader
scene lists from a file
nodes.note: the raw files on D: (json tables, maps, CAM_FRONT, radars; data/NuScenes/ describes and checks them), the light reader (the tables of just the sequences asked for, cached), and the scene lists: a list of sequences comes from a file (--scenes-file) or is a shipped set (small = the 10 mini sequences, full = all 850); a list is named by the id of its content

nodes.label: Tests: python -m GtGenerator selftest
nodes.note: synthetic world with known truth, real keyframes, build + reload; every command is one method and one call; exact raster against the polygons; generator against the devkit, the map and the image; lane graph invariants; the signature guard; each new test is checked by a mutant; this drawing is checked against the code
